item.text: I’ll read the selected lyric, reconstruct the Urdu verses from its Roman transcription, and check that the two editions align.

item.aggregated_output:
---
title: "کہتے تھے یہ عباسؑ سکینہؑ سے یہ دلبر"
language: "Urdu"
lang: "ur"
direction: "ltr"
kalamType: "Noha"
reciter: "Tanzeem-ul-Husaini (Nasir Zaidi)"
tags: ["noUrdu"]
aliases: []
published: false
---

Kehtay thay ye Abbas Sakina se ke dilbar
De do hamay mashkeeza abhi latay hain bhar kar

1
Bas itna karam haal pe Ammo ke ye kar do
Baba se riza ran ki dila do hamain ja kar

2
Ye suntay ke mashkeeza Sakina ne uthaya
Pohonchi liye Ammo ko huzoor e Shah e Safdar

3
Seenay se lipat jao chacha ke karo rukhsat
Tab jayain sooye nehr teri mashk ko le kar

4
Ho jaye agar dair to ghabrana na bibi
Pani abhi layain gay jo aa jaye mayassar

5
Tum tarrpo gi ya ro gi ya noha karo gi
Ham bhi wahan din raat guzarain gay tarrap kar

6
Parrhtay huay ye Noha alam laye sheh e deen
Matam karo maray gaye Abbas e dilawar

7
Woh soz day nohay ko Anees aap ke Zainab
Sun le to kaleja phatay ronay lagay pathar

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = Path(\"src/data/lyrics/kehte-the-ye-abbas-sakina-se-ke-dilbar.md\")
old = subprocess.check_output([\"git\", \"show\", f\"HEAD:{p}\"], text=True)
_, meta, source = p.read_text().split(\"---\\n\", 2)
roman = \"\\n\".join(line.removeprefix(\"  \") for line in meta.split(\"romanLyrics: |-\\n\", 1)[1].splitlines()).strip()
assert roman == old.split(\"---\\n\", 2)[2].strip()
for edition, digits in [(roman, \"1234567\"), (source, \"۱۲۳۴۵۶۷\")]:
    blocks = [block.splitlines() for block in edition.strip().split(\"\\n\\n\")]
    assert len(blocks) == 8 and len(blocks[0]) == 2
    assert all(len(block) == 3 and block[0] == digit for block, digit in zip(blocks[1:], digits))
assert source.count(\"\\u200c\") == source.count(\"بی\\u200cبی\") == 1
print(\"Roman wording unchanged; both editions have a two-verse opening and seven two-verse stanzas.\")
PY
git diff --check -- src/data/lyrics/kehte-the-ye-abbas-sakina-se-ke-dilbar.md"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 16 Urdu verses in the [selected lyric](/home/ghayur/.local/state/kalam-codex-round2/shards/2/workspaces/6657bfec4c5f4f778de82a8d952ab45b/src/data/lyrics/kehte-the-ye-abbas-sakina-se-ke-dilbar.md) and preserved the original Roman transcription in `romanLyrics`. Verified that the opening and all seven stanzas align. Set the direction to RTL and removed `noUrdu`.

I corrected the second `یہ` in the title to `کہ` to match the opening verse, and read “ran” as `رَن` and “alam” as `علم` in context.
